title: Early Church Persecution
content: Early Christians faced persecution under several Roman emperors. Refusing to worship the emperor or Roman gods often resulted in imprisonment or execution. Despite persecution, Christianity spread rapidly throughout the Roman Empire and many believers remained faithful even under suffering.

title: Church Fathers and Apostolic Authority
content: The early Church Fathers were Christian leaders who lived shortly after the apostles. Some were disciples of the apostles themselves. Their writings confirm core Christian doctrines such as the divinity of Christ, the resurrection, and the authority of Scripture.

title: Spread of Christianity
content: Christianity spread rapidly through preaching, missionary journeys, and strong Christian communities. The message of salvation through Jesus Christ crossed cultural and social boundaries, reaching Jews and Gentiles throughout the Roman Empire.

title: Early Church Councils and Doctrinal Clarity
content: Early church councils were gatherings of Christian leaders who addressed doctrinal questions and defended the faith against false teachings. The Council of Nicaea in AD 325 affirmed the full divinity of Jesus Christ and helped establish clear Christian doctrine.
